about: Film-ready recipes for the one-command launch film. in/out: the part of the shot's 1920x1080 render that goes into the film, in seconds of the source film. They cut each shot before its own wordmark, except the Ending, which keeps it. needs: what the shot is filled with. text = a line or paragraph of the product's copy; ui = one product screen rebuilt in HTML; logo = the product's mark and name. theme: the source's background (dark or light); prefer shots whose theme matches the brand, since switching a dark shot to a light brand (or back) is real work. note: what to watch when adapting.

shots.fits: a product with a sharp one-paragraph claim
developer tools, CLIs, anything driven by a prompt or command
a bold wordmark, design or creative products
a desktop or web product with two or three named features, each a one-word headline
shots.note: Each headline word must name the feature shown in the window on the same frame. The words and the window content are the product's own; keep every word narrower than the window so it can sink fully behind the top edge. The source ends on its own wordmark after 8.2s, which the film cuts.

shots.fits: a launch with one feature headline that names a capability, design and creative tools, 3D or perspective features
shots.note: Cut at 5.05s, the frame where the wipe band covers the screen; the film's own editor UI and wordmark after it are left out, and the user's real product UI follows. The title rises from under its mask from frame 0, so the cut starts at 0.1s, after the first empty frames. The title copy is two lines and the band copy is a four-word arrow list, so both need replacing with the product's own words.

shots.fits: a product with one short claim and several distinct screens, such as workspaces, suites and AI assistants
shots.note: Opens on a light screen (the doc) and alternates light and dark through the word section (0 to 4.7s, light on words 1, 3, 5 and 7) and through the four caption shots (4.7 to 6.8s, light, dark, light, dark), so the theme is mixed and the opening frame is light. The word color flips with each screen. Use the product's own screens, one word per cut, 0.5s per word (0.7s after a comma, 0.9s for the last word); a longer line adds one screen per word and keeps 0.5s holds. The captions (4.7 to 6.8s) are optional: out can move to 4.7 to end on the last word. The cream card and wordmark after 6.8s belong to the source's own ending and are cut.

shots.fits: hardware or a glossy product with a dense screen, where a light sweep can open the film and then cross the product name
shots.note: Replace the watch and its face with the product's own device or main screen, and the title with its name. The flare is drawn by code from one source position, so change only the path, timing and colours: keep the ghosts on the line through the source and the frame centre. The excerpt runs through the title fade-out and ends before the lockup at 7.85s.

shots.fits: a release, changelog or version launch told as a story, developer tools, anything with a short announcement paragraph
shots.note: Cut at 9.2s, before the crawl fades and the film's own lockup appears. The intro line, the kicker, the title and the three paragraphs are the product's own words: keep each paragraph near 21 words so the block is about 16 lines and the last line reaches the bottom edge by about 9s, and keep the blue accent only for the intro line and the kicker. The scene has no UI, so the next shot supplies the product screen. Use no film names, logos or the classic crawl yellow.

shots.fits: any product with a dense, good-looking main screen
search, command bars, lists, AI answers
hardware, displays or any product whose key claim is one short word or number; the word is revealed through glass ribs
shots.note: The word is one text block copied into 28 ribs; keep it to 3-4 heavy letters (Inter 800, about 330px cap height on the 1092px screen). The laptop is a CSS 3D model: keep it for hardware, or drop it and run the ribs full-frame for software. Cut at 4.7s, before the push-in and the film's own Novis Pro lockup.

shots.fits: a product with a dense main screen on a device, where the surrounding space can be made of its other screens: analytics, dashboards, feeds, mobile apps with a web counterpart
shots.note: Animate only the perspective distance and keep the subject on z=0 so it never changes size. The windows around the subject and the wall at the end must be the product's own screens. The first lockup frame is at 6.2s, so the cut ends before it.

shots.fits: a product whose pitch rests on numbers: speed, savings, uptime or volume, with a dashboard screen to show them
shots.note: Replace the three stats with the product's own numbers (a multiplier, a currency amount that counts from a lower start, a percentage) and the dashboard with its real screen; keep the digit count and the count end values consistent with each label. The odometer needs one value per card and a fixed-width column per digit. Cut at 7.5s, before the film's own lockup.

shots.fits: a hardware product with a layered build (glass, display, board, battery, back) and two or three spec lines to call out: phones, wearables, laptops, cameras
shots.note: Replace the phone and its seven layers with the product's own parts, keeping the three top layers (glass, display, frame) separate from the inner ones so they can fade out for the board close-up; the lock screen is the product's own screen and the three callouts take real part names and specs. The layers are drawn in code (SVG and CSS), so only artwork, labels and the pivot target on the main chip change. The cut ends at 8.4s, before the lockup, with the layers still closing and the phone already sliding right, so the next shot should open on the finished product.

shots.fits: a product with a dense main screen and a few small notification, approval or insight cards, plus a one-line headline: finance, ops, analytics and team tools
shots.note: Replace the laptop dashboard with the product's own main screen and the two foreground cards with two of its real notifications or cards (each about 700px wide before scaling); the headline takes one short two-line claim. Keep one card in frame per rack, as the source does. The cut ends at 9.1s, before the scene fades and the source's own lockup.

shots.fits: one concrete action in the UI: a button, a field, a drag
two short spec or benefit lines
shots.note: The source sets the words around a 3D camera lens. Replace the lens with the product's own object or remove it; never keep a prop the product does not have.

shots.fits: grids of items: templates, fonts, files, styles
AI products with a prompt box
products that clear a backlog or automate a chore
hardware or a product with several app screens and one headline spec
shots.note: The beams carry the product's own screens: replace the editor, console and mail screens with its UI and keep the laptop only if the product ships a device (otherwise use its app icon on the lid). The stat on the wide beam takes one short claim in three parts on the right edge: a small line, a large number and a label. The excerpt ends before the lid closes and the wordmark.

shots.fits: AI writing, voice, notes and summary features: a long input that the product condenses into one short result
shots.note: Replace the dictated line with the product's own long input and the bubble text with its short output; keep the 36 words to 10 counter and the Summarized by line consistent with the new copy. The shot ends on a chat window that is fully visible until 8.65s; the window fade and the Gist lockup after 8.65 are cut.

shots.fits: an AI product with a chat or prompt box that builds, writes or edits something visible next to it: app builders, coding agents, design, data and automation tools
shots.note: Replace the prompt, the three tool-step titles with their subtitles, the reply sentence and the preview dashboard with the product's own (the preview is one screen rebuilt in HTML). Keep the camera tight on the chat column until the result appears, then pull back once. The cut ends at 8.2s, before the window fades and the source's own lockup.

shots.fits: several states of one element: before and after, many outputs
themes, styles, fonts, templates
shots.note: The reskinned page must be the product's own screen; do not put the product inside an editor it does not have.

shots.fits: products with nested content: projects, folders, docs, boards, threads
shots.note: Needs four of the product's own screens where a card or embedded view on each one shows the next, and the last one embeds the first. Keep the preview rectangle at 16:9 and rebuild all four screens before changing the zoom numbers.

shots.fits: any product that organizes visual items (boards, galleries, libraries, files) and wants to move from one screen to the next
shots.note: Needs 15 content cards (images, color, type, screens, notes) from the product's own material, each 240x320 with a back face; the board window is rebuilt from the product's real screen. Cut before the veil at 7.7s; the lockup after it is the film's own wordmark.

shots.fits: a camera, photo or video product, or any launch with two or three screens to join in one move
shots.note: Needs three of the product's own screens and a two-line headline for the first one. Cut at 8.3s, the frame where the third leak is brightest; the lockup after it is the film's own and is left out, so the next shot should open from a bright frame. The leak colors stay orange, amber and magenta on any brand; replace only the amber UI accent (#ff9a2e). Keep each cut inside the 0.08s plateau where the flash is at 0.98.

shots.fits: going from a headline claim to the product itself
shots.note: Replace the two-line headline (88px, about 13 characters per line fits inside the 380px ring), the product scene (it is built once by a function and copied into the five reveal circles, so change it in one place), the spec line and the accent #8fb4ff. Cut before the product recedes at 7.3s; the lockup after it is the film's own wordmark.

shots.fits: a product with a fast, noisy world around it and one precise claim: sensors, audio, trading, health, live events
shots.note: Replace scene A (0 to 3.5s) with the product's own busiest moment, such as many cards moving, charts racing or a live feed, and keep it moving and getting closer until the cut at 3.5s (frame 105); the 9 strobes and the BPM card belong to the crowd and can go. The claim is two centred lines at 72px (3 words each; for a longer claim keep two lines and reserve every word's space) typing in at 0.2s per word with a 1s pause between the lines. Replace the green LEDs and the sensor plate with the product's hero object, lit between the two lines, and swap the accent #34e27a for the brand color. The lockup after 7.6s is the source's own and is cut.

shots.fits: default ending
shots.note: Mark size, push scale, lockup offsets and letter positions are computed for a 4-letter name and a 252x160 mark. Recompute them from the product's mark and the measured width of its name.

shots.fits: products that bring many pieces together
event endings with a date and URL
shots.note: The mark and the 10 characters of the wordmark are hand-built stroke paths (arcs and lines, x-height 100 units) with a skeleton pass and a fill pass each; for another name rebuild the glyph paths, the pen start times and the camera targets (keep the pen tip near the middle of the frame: aim the camera at the tip in take 1 and a little left of the active letter in take 3). Set pathLength to 10000 because GSAP rounds CSS lengths and a pathLength of 1 would make strokes jump. Keep the ending date and URL short, about 11 and 14 characters. Keep the paper light; the ink and one accent color come from the brand.

shots.fits: products that sell clarity, focus or speed and want to end on a one-line promise
shots.note: Replace line 3 and the tagline (keep the tagline to about 14 characters: 184px type fills about 1420px of the frame), the accent #ffb15c, the 108px mark and the 9-letter wordmark Clearline, and the editor behind the text with the product's own screen. Keep the screen's blur-to-sharp timing (5.6–6.9s) on the third line and the tagline rise (8.7s) before the mark.
